name: ESM protein language models (Meta FAIR, then EvolutionaryScale, now Biohub)
subcategory: protein language models, structure prediction and generative protein design
origin_detail: Built by Meta's FAIR Protein Team (ESM-1 to ESM-2/ESMFold, 2019-2022). The team spun out as EvolutionaryScale (public benefit company; ESM3 2024-06-25, ESM C 2024-12), which is now part of the non-profit Chan Zuckerberg Biohub (per E/evolutionaryscale.json). The repos now sit under the Biohub GitHub organisation, and Meta's repo was archived as Biohub/esm-archive on 2026-11-20.

licences.code: MIT (Meta, 2019-2022) -> EvolutionaryScale terms (2024) -> MIT (2026-05-27, copyright Chan Zuckerberg Biohub)
licences.weights: MIT (Meta ESM-2) -> ESM3 Community / Cambrian Non-Commercial (ESM3-open, ESM C 600M), Cambrian Open (ESM C 300M) -> MIT (2026); 98B ESM3 not released
licences.data: ESM Atlas CC BY 4.0; trained on UniRef (public)

openness_notes: Meta era: source MIT; the ESM Metagenomic Atlas (617 million predicted structures, Nov 2022, about 150M more in Mar 2023) is CC BY 4.0 'for academic and commercial use'. ESM-2 weights are MIT on Hugging Face; the Meta repo does not state a separate weights licence. EvolutionaryScale era: ESM3 (2024-06-25) was trained with over 1e24 FLOPs at 98B parameters, but only a 1.4B open model was released. Per the 2025-01-16 LICENSE.md, ESM3-open and ESM C 600M were under the Cambrian Non-Commercial License (based on the original ESM3 Community License), and ESM C 300M under the more permissive Cambrian Open License. The commercial route was a paid API. The only later change to LICENSE.md (2026-05-27) replaced these terms with MIT, copyright Chan Zuckerberg Biohub (2026). Initial 3 (MIT code and weights, public training data); trough 1 (2024); current 2 (open small models, the 98B ESM3 not released).

openness_effect_assessment: Meta's MIT-licensed ESM-2 is among the most-used science models (3.0M HF downloads a month for one size). The restricted ESM3-open drew about 2.3k a month. When the team left Meta for a VC-backed company, the licence closed (non-commercial, API for the frontier model); after it joined a non-profit, the open models returned to MIT.
key_takeaway: Openness tracked the owner's incentives: open at Meta, restricted at a VC-backed startup, open again under a philanthropic non-profit. Download counts show how much more the permissive models were used.
